questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: One of the most crucial aspects in choosing New Zealand as my study destination was its strong tradition and international reputation within outdoor education and environmental studies, which aligns closely with my academic and personal interests. In addition, the country’s unique natural environment offered a valuable opportunity to experience learning in direct connection with diverse landscapes and ecosystems. Finally, the cultural dimension, including the chance to gain insights into Māori perspectives and ways of relating to nature, was an important factor that made New Zealand a particularly meaningful destination for me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The teaching was highly engaging and practice-oriented, combining theoretical knowledge with hands-on learning in the field. I especially valued the balance between academic depth and experiential approaches, which created a strong connection between the classroom and the natural environment.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process at my host institution was quite challenging at times. The time difference made communication slower and more difficult, as responses often took several days. In addition, there were many different steps to complete before receiving confirmation, which made the process feel lengthy and a bit complicated.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student service, but they were hard to get in contact with.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Because the application process starts very early on, some of the classes I was hoping for, ended up not being offeret that semester. Furthermore it was difficult to get the courses pre-approved by my own university.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Contact the primary educational coordinator well in advance and talk to them about the options for your classes. And start well in advance with everything. It takes so so so long. And there is always more to do, before the process is done.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: One of the most challenging cultural differences was adapting to the more indirect communication style, which sometimes made it harder to understand expectations. Additionally, the time difference to Europe made staying connected with home more difficult.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: their love for nature.
